allowed_dependency_manifest.content: For each fixed integer n at least 2, consider all sign sequences of length n minus 1 with entries plus or minus 1. Define f(s) as the number of permutations of {1, 2, ..., n} whose consecutive differences have the prescribed signs. The task is to identify exactly which sign sequences s maximize f(s).

forbidden_claims.statement_nl: Let $n$ be an integer with $n \\geq 2$. For a sequence $s = (s_1,\\dots,s_{n-1})$ where each $s_i = \\pm 1$, let $f(s)$ be the number of permutations $(a_1,\\dots,a_n)$ of $\\{1,2,\\dots,n\\}$ such that $s_i(a_{i+1}-a_i) > 0$ for all $i$. For each $n$, determine the sequences $s$ for which $f(s)$ is maximal.

statement_nl: Fix an integer n >= 2. For each integer r >= 1, let E_r be the number of permutations (b_1,...,b_r) of {1,...,r} such that (-1)^(i-1) * (b_{i+1} - b_i) > 0 for every 1 <= i <= r-1, and set E_0 = 1. Define w_j = binom(n-1, j-1) * E_{j-1} * E_{n-j} for 1 <= j <= n, define S_odd = sum over odd j in {1,...,n} of w_j, and define S_even = sum over even j in {1,...,n} of w_j. If P is a subset of {1,...,n} containing no two consecutive integers, then sum over j in P of w_j is at most max(S_odd, S_even). If, in addition, S_odd = S_even, then equality sum over j in P of w_j = max(S_odd, S_even) holds if and only if P is exactly the set of odd integers in {1,...,n} or exactly the set of even integers in {1,...,n}.
